[SELECTED WORK]{.eyebrow}

## Research & academic highlights

A selection of projects exploring public opinion, political communication, and international affairs.

::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}
[PUBLIC OPINION & GOVERNANCE]{.project-label}

### Understanding the Angeleno Outlook

Longitudinal research using Angeleno Poll data to examine institutional trust, regional pessimism, and community belonging in Los Angeles.

[Explore research](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.research-card}
[INTERNATIONAL RELATIONS & FINANCE]{.project-label}

### When Words Become Risk

An undergraduate honors thesis investigating whether geopolitical threat rhetoric influences safe-haven currency markets and exchange-rate volatility.

[Explore research](research.qmd)
:::

::: {.research-card}
[POLITICAL COMMUNICATION & TEXT ANALYSIS]{.project-label}

### Analyzing Trump's 2019 Tweets

A computational text analysis project applying sentiment analysis and topic modeling to examine political communication surrounding the proposed border wall.

[View research poster](files/research_poster.html)
:::

## Questions worth asking

I'm interested in how political institutions, public narratives, and international events shape our world. By combining quantitative methods with social science research, I work to turn complex questions into rigorous, evidence-based projects.

My academic interests extend beyond the classroom. Through government internships, public opinion research, conference presentations, and student leadership, I seek opportunities to apply research to real-world challenges and better understand the communities and institutions around us.
